In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the condylomata are a preneoplastic lesion.
there is no proof of a direct causal relationship between condyloma acuminata and Bowen’s disease.
the wart cells of the condylomata are not the origin of the carcinoma in situ but the latter is derived from the basal layer of the squamous epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ultrastructure of condylomata is not pathognomonic, that the wart cells of condylomatus acuminata are not identical with the cells of the morbus Bowen, but that the wart cells are a possible precursor of the cells of the Bowen's disease.
the wart cells of condylomata develop from basal cells of the epidermis, that they are not derived from the stratum malpighii, and that the virus is located in the cell nuclei of the wart cells.
the wart cells are not able to transform themselves into carcinoma cells without an additional influence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current understanding of the mechanisms of HPV-induced carcinogenesis is not sufficient to explain the development of HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV-OPSCC) and that further studies are required to understand the mechanisms of this disease.
